title: Create signed kernel-bundle artifacts and runtime verification flow for GPU runtime
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem:
Across recent upgrades (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS) we've seen intermittent runtime failures and silent correctness regressions caused by mismatched kernel binaries and non-deterministic CI builds. These issues are particularly painful for Dedicated and Private customers where images are staged across regions and offline.

Goal:
Produce deterministic, signed kernel-bundle artifacts for each supported model/runtime combo and add a lightweight verification step in the runtime loader to ensure only validated bundles are used. This reduces risk from accidental ABI mismatches, improves incident triage (hash + signature in logs), and enables safe rollout of kernel updates.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In-scope: CI build determinism, artifact signing pipeline, runtime verification and logging, fallback policy to prior verified bundle, basic rollout integration in Console.
- Out-of-scope: hardware attestation/HSM-integration for customer-provided private deployments (separate follow-up), full supply-chain provenance (SBOMs are handled by another initiative).

Deliverables:
1) CI pipeline changes to produce deterministic kernel-bundle tar.gz with embedded metadata (version map, SHA256, build-id) for each CUTLASS/Triton variant.
2) Signing service (initially using internal signing key stored in vault) that produces detached signatures and a bundle manifest file.
3) Runtime loader change: verify signature and hash before loading kernel libs; on failure fall back to verified local bundle if available and emit structured logs and metrics.
4) Console/Deploy integration: show bundle hash + signature verification results in model rollout UI and allow explicit pinning to signed bundle.
5) Test matrix and synthetic smoke tests to validate loading, fallback, and telemetry.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- Use deterministic build flags and hermetic build env to remove non-determinism. This increases CI time slightly but is acceptable for release artifacts.
- Initial signing will use a team-managed key in Vault; long-term plan is to integrate with HSM/KMS per security roadmap.
- Verification in runtime must be minimal overhead; signature check occurs once per process start or on hot-swap, not per request.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary builds): produce signed bundles and add non-blocking verification that logs mismatches (no runtime rejection).
- Phase 2 (soft enforcement): reject unsigned bundles in non-critical fleets and run SW rollback tests.
- Phase 3 (enforce): runtime refuses to load unsigned/tainted bundles except under explicit operator override.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Number of kernel-mismatch incidents drops to zero for signed fleets within 2 months of enforcement.
- Time to diagnose kernel-related failures reduced by >=50% via logged artifact hashes.
- No measurable startup latency increase (>5%) for verified startups.

Security / compliance:
- Security review required before Phase 2.
- Signing keys provisioned via Vault access controls; audit logs enabled.

Tasks (high level):
- T1: Design deterministic build spec and manifest format (Ava, 2d).
- T2: CI changes to produce artifact and manifest (Eng Build Team, 5d).
- T3: Implement signing service and key lifecycle docs (Infra Sec, 4d).
- T4: Runtime loader verification and fallback logic (Runtime Team, 7d).
- T5: Console integration for bundle metadata (Console Team, 3d).
- T6: E2E tests + canary rollout (SRE, 5d).

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: Deterministic builds may still have hidden non-determinism (linker timestamps, host toolchain). Mitigation: canonical build container and reproducibility tests.
- Risk: Signing key compromise. Mitigation: restrict access, enable audit trails, rotate keys and support revocation list in runtime.
- Risk: Customers with custom kernels (private deploy) may be blocked. Mitigation: provide operator override and documented onboarding flow for customer-signed bundles.

Related artifacts / links:
- RFC: Confluence (internal) - signed-kernel-proposal (link placeholder)
- CI PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3942
- Observability dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kernelevents

QA / Test plan:
- Unit tests for manifest parsing and signature verification.
- Integration test: build deterministically in CI, verify signature accepted in runtime image.
- Regression test: ensure fallback path works and that metrics emit properly.
- Load test: verify no more than 5% startup overhead on p3/4-equivalent instances.

Notes:
- For rollout transparency, each log line for kernel load will include bundle-id, hash, signer-id and verification result. This will be searchable by support and included in SLO alerting rules.
- Targeting runtime-1.20 for soft enforcement, with post-release monitoring window of 8 weeks.
